content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Background

Several recent provider moves, reported between August and the end of October 2026, concern settings that sit between a developer's code and a model: sampling parameters, text watermarks, model selection and the agent harness. This analysis lays them side by side and records, for each, what the cited sources say about who decides. The grouping and the table below are the Herald's own; each cell is drawn from a cited source.

editor_notes.content_quality: Genuine Analysis: it compares four provider/developer control points (sampling parameters, text watermarks, model routing, agent harness) rather than recapping one release. Structure is Background / Current situation / table / Implications; reported facts are attributed to named outlets or vendor documents, and the grouping and table are explicitly flagged as the Herald's own. Implications are labelled as following from what is reported, with no forecast or opinion. Title is exactly 140 characters (cap 150). Word count 1,378 with link URLs stripped (range 800-2000).
editor_notes.source_verification: Read all 8 snapshots from disk (source-0..7.html.gz, all HTTP 200, no archive fallback, no sponsored label found in any). Hosts checked by exact hostname: thenewstack.io, devblogs.microsoft.com, the-decoder.com, techcrunch.com, platform.claude.com - all on the allowlist, no edits needed. ANALYSIS INDEPENDENCE COUNT: 3 independent outlets (The New Stack, The Decoder, TechCrunch) covering 6 of the 8 cited URLs, plus 2 first-party (devblogs.microsoft.com Foundry post; platform.claude.com migration guide). Requirement (>=4 sources, >=2 independent) met. Honest recount of independence: source-0 New Stack (Microsoft harness) is an original news/analysis piece with its own 'Runtime limits and lock-in' section; source-2 New Stack (Jassy) reports the Q3 2026 earnings call and adds its own commentary; source-3 New Stack (Copilot Fusion) largely relays GitHub's statements and benchmark claims ('Per GitHub', 'GitHub reports'), and I count it as partly independent only; the article uses it for attributed description and calls the figures self-reported, which is accurate. source-4 The Decoder (Matthias Bastian, Oct 31 2026) is original reporting on an Anthropic email to API customers with outside voices (Gruber, Artificial Lawyer). source-5 TechCrunch (Aditya Mehta, Oct 5 2026) and source-6 TechCrunch (Ivan Mehta, Aug 11 2026) are reporting built on OpenAI's blog post and Anthropic's support page respectively, by an independent outlet, with TechCrunch's own context. Claim-by-claim: source-7 migration guide: 'returns a 400 error, even at the parameter's default value' verbatim; 'such as Claude 4.7 and later models' and Sonnet 4.6 lowered-temperature effect confirmed; the page contains zero mentions of 'watermark'. source-4: Mythos 5 / Opus 4.7 / Opus 4.6 / Sonnet 4.6 list, Opus 5.5 already marked, watermark only at default temperature/top_p/top_k on Opus 4.6 and Sonnet 4.6, quote 'If you rely on the watermark for your own compliance, keep these settings at their defaults.' verbatim, no caveat for Mythos 5/Opus 4.7 (Decoder's inference, correctly attributed as 'which it reads as'), model-level so works on AWS/Google Cloud/Foundry, 'Customers can't turn it off', textGrain disabled by default for API, 'is disputed' with Gruber and Artificial Lawyer - all confirmed. source-5: EU rules took effect Aug 2, ChatGPT and Codex EU only, API anywhere can turn on for select models, off by default, 'the instructions, context, decisions' and 'the tool' backlash quotes verbatim. source-6: models released after Aug 2, text and files, older models to follow, 'applied at the model level' confirmed (full quote: 'Watermarking will be applied at the model level'). source-3: 'choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you.' verbatim; Standard/High/Max; administrators can disable models for Fusion; score 60 within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max at about half the cost; article dated Oct 28 (GitHub Universe, Wednesday). source-2: Jassy on Amazon's Q3 2026 earnings call (Thursday, article dated Oct 31): 'most customers are going to use multiple models, and many will use multiple models in the same generative AI application.' and 'swap them back and forth as they leapfrog each other, as different constraints of their applications require them.' verbatim, speaker and event correct; switching/test/harness caution is New Stack's own text and is attributed to 'the same article'. source-0 (Oct 29): 'must be selected when creating a prompt agent, and that choice can't be changed later, even in a new version' and 'isn't supported with the managed Copilot harness' verbatim. source-1 Microsoft post: 'switching the harness after creation isn't supported yet', 'a supported Foundry model', hosted agents bring own framework etc., billing from December 1, 2026 with free runtime before - confirmed. KEY RISK 1 (table placements): every row traces to a cited source and the table intro marks the grouping as the Herald's own; the Foundry row and sampling row are first-party-sourced and labelled so. KEY RISK 2 (open question): the Decoder says the watermark applies on Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 only at default settings, and the migration guide says sending the three parameters at any value, default included, returns a 400 on API version 2026-10-21; neither source discusses the interaction, so 'neither cited source says how the removal interacts with the watermark condition' is accurate and fairly stated (the guide also says the version is Bedrock-available only for Claude 4.7+, so the article does not overreach). The Herald's two internal links resolve to published articles (2026-10/31-anthropic-api-version-2026-10-21-... and 2026-10/08-openai-will-watermark-...) and are described accurately. Orphan-link diff: every body URL is in article.sources and vice versa (chief:review 'body sources match' pass). editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No fabricated specifics found. One imprecision: the article says Ramp 'described moving model selection into its open-source coding agent Open SWE this month'; the New Stack piece is dated Oct 28 and means October, while the article is published Nov 1, so 'this month' now reads as November. Handled with a clarification. Source dates are stated honestly (TechCrunch Aug 11 and Oct 5; Decoder Oct 31; New Stack Oct 28 for Fusion; Microsoft post read on Nov 1). The statement that the reporting does not say whether developers can see which model handled a request is an absence claim; I searched source-3 and found nothing on routing visibility, so it holds.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral. Nothing about Anthropic is promotional or disparaging beyond the sources: every Anthropic statement is attributed to The Decoder, TechCrunch or Anthropic's own migration guide, and the Decoder's remark that Opus 4.6 is Anthropic's best writing model was correctly left out. The Implications section stays within what the sources show.
editor_notes.originality: The Herald previously published the API 2026-10-21 report (Oct 31) and the OpenAI watermark report (Oct 8), both linked for continuity; no published article compares these controls across providers. Also related: the Oct 28 Copilot Fusion GA changelog article. New angle, not a duplicate.
editor_notes.conflict_of_interest: The article centrally concerns Anthropic's own controls (removal of sampling parameters in API version 2026-10-21, the model-level watermark, the Opus 4.6/Sonnet 4.6 default-settings condition). Anthropic makes the Claude models that power this newsroom's writer and reviewer. Disclosed here and, consistent with the earlier Bun/agent-rewrite review, a reader-facing clarification is filed in the corrections record. Attribution to third-party outlets and Anthropic's own documents was verified as above.
concerns: Anthropic is a central subject and also makes the models used by this newsroom; a clarification discloses this.
The Fusion New Stack article largely relays GitHub's claims; the article labels those figures as self-reported and does not rely on it as independent confirmation.
'This month' for the Ramp item is ambiguous given the Nov 1 publication date (clarification filed).
editor_notes.overall_assessment: A well-sourced, properly bounded Analysis that meets all of the Analysis requirements (1,378 words, 8 sources, 3 independent outlets, a topic examined across several developments, facts separated from analysis). Approved with a corrections record holding two clarifications. Featured candidacy: 1 - accurate cross-provider comparison useful to developers who depend on sampling settings, routers and managed harnesses, but a defined audience and not an industry-changing story
